source.title: De-randomized PAC-Bayes Margin Bounds: Applications to Non-convex and Non-smooth Predictors
source.authors: Arindam Banerjee; Tiancong Chen; Yingxue Zhou

record.tranche_reason: The study varies label randomness and training set size, then reports test error and how its proposed bound components change. These results bear on V1’s natural-versus-random label setting, but do not report the specific chance-level comparison in that version.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-error trends for label-randomness and training-set-size sweeps. It does not report the specific random-label test accuracy or training error figures needed to establish V1’s stated comparison.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own label-corruption experiments and explicitly states that training error remains zero as label randomness increases. This tests V1's memorization-capacity component, although corruption stops at 50% and the supplied text does not establish the complete natural-label versus fully random-label held-out comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate as an attribution: the authors claim their de-randomized bounds show the expected qualitative responses to label corruption and sample size and are meaningful and non-vacuous. Qualify the numerical claim: the displayed experimental bounds omit additive terms, as Section 5.1 explicitly states; quantitative sharpening remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates de-randomized PAC-Bayes margin bounds; its empirical setups use fully connected ReLU networks and Adam. It does not reproduce the original study’s memorization/generalization experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported bound components and bound vary with label-randomness fraction and training-set size; experiments also vary depth, width, dataset, and batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error increases as training-label corruption increases; effective curvature, weight-norm terms, margin loss, and the displayed bound also increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial label corruption worsens held-out performance and increases the proposed bound components in the tested fully connected ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error decreases with increasing training-set size on both MNIST and CIFAR-10, alongside decreases in the displayed bound and its scaled components.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing training-set size improves held-out performance and lowers the proposed bound in these experiments.

record.problems: Most experimental results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The reported measurements are for selected fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10; the text does not establish the chance-level random-label test accuracy required by V1.
record.rows_left_out: No additional test-error rows extracted for the other architecture and sample-size sweeps described in Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix E: many panels are figure-only and the text does not separately describe their test-error direction. Bound-component and bound values were excluded because they do not measure the test error or generalization gap named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, chance-level held-out accuracy under complete randomization, and a readable above-chance natural-label accuracy comparison. The experiments randomize at most 50% of labels.
Test-error changes from widening beyond the interpolation threshold; separate widths are presented without establishing this comparison.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent differences.
Large-batch penalties under matched epoch budgets and recipe adaptations; batch sizes 16 and 128 alone do not establish this comparison.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures. Diagonal Hessian curvature and a PAC-Bayes bound are different measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples.

missing.what: Zero training error despite increasing label corruption. Add training-error rows alongside the test-error rows; the current gate note incorrectly says training-fit evidence is unavailable.
missing.locator: Introduction Sections 1.2–1.3, summarizing the Section 5 experiments

record.verdict_notes: Remove the extracted limits_scope verdict: an unmeasured chance-level comparison is an untested part, not evidence that V1 fails. The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values, so exact accuracies cannot be reconstructed.

versions.untested_parts: The text reports test error increasing as label randomness increases, but does not give exact test-error values, state that random-label test accuracy is at chance, or separately report natural-label accuracy far above chance alongside near-perfect random-label training fit.

The paper measures diagonal Hessian curvature and uses it in a PAC-Bayes bound, but does not test magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or compare its ranking of generalization gaps with the measures named in V7.
